diagrams.title: Pyoderma Gangrenosum Diagnostic Workup
diagrams.subtitle: Biopsy supports the diagnosis and excludes mimics; it does not independently prove PG

items.label: Rapid painful evolution from papule, pustule, nodule, or bulla
Pathergy after minor trauma, surgery, ostomy manipulation, or debridement
Associated IBD, inflammatory arthritis, hematologic disease, monoclonal gammopathy, malignancy, or prior PG
Medication and exposure review; assess cocaine/levamisole, warfarin/heparin, vasopressors, and injectable injury when relevant

stages.name: 2 · Examine morphology and the whole patient

items.label: Violaceous, undermined, tender border with inflammatory expansion
Purulent-appearing or necrotic base is not itself proof of infection
Classify classic ulcerative, bullous, pustular, vegetative, peristomal, or postoperative phenotype
Assess pulses, edema, livedo/retiform change, neuropathy, and pressure distribution
Deep incisional or punch biopsy from active ulcer edge including subcutis
items.detail: The major criterion in Delphi criteria is neutrophilic infiltration at the ulcer edge. The biopsy also excludes vasculitis, malignancy, calciphylaxis, infection, and other ulcer causes.

items.label: Send separate tissue for bacterial, fungal, and mycobacterial culture when indicated
Additional testing guided by differential
items.detail: CBC/CMP, inflammatory markers, SPEP/IFE, vascular studies, coagulation/APS testing, cryoglobulins, or imaging are not universal panels; select from phenotype.

items.label: Use Delphi or PARACELSUS criteria as structured support—not a substitute for exclusion of dangerous mimics.
Monitor border inflammation, pain, ulcer area, granulation, and new lesions. Healing can lag behind control of inflammatory progression.
Failure or paradoxical worsening
items.detail: Re-culture/re-biopsy and reconsider infection, vascular occlusion, calciphylaxis, malignancy, factitial disease, and incorrect wound care.

citations.quote: International Delphi criteria for ulcerative pyoderma gangrenosum combine an ulcer-edge neutrophilic biopsy with validated clinical minor criteria.
Review classifies neutrophilic dermatoses by clinical and histopathologic pattern and emphasizes exclusion of infection and systemic associations.

diagrams.title: Systemic Association Workup
diagrams.subtitle: Target evaluation to phenotype, age, laboratory abnormalities, and recurrence

stages.name: 1 · Minimum assessment for a new significant neutrophilic eruption

items.label: Medication, infection, inflammatory disease, cancer, pregnancy, and recent procedure/trauma history
Full skin/mucosal examination, lymph nodes, joints, abdomen, ocular symptoms, and targeted organ review
CBC with differential, CMP, and inflammatory markers when systemic disease is possible
Sweet/bullous Sweet, anemia/cytopenias, constitutional symptoms
items.detail: Peripheral smear; hematology review; marrow evaluation only when indicated by clinical/laboratory concern.

items.label: PG or subcorneal pustular disease
items.detail: IBD review; arthritis evaluation; SPEP/IFE/free light chains when age/phenotype suggests gammopathy.

items.label: NUD with recurrent fever, bone pain, arthralgia, or high CRP
items.detail: Assess Still disease, Schnitzler syndrome, CAPS/other autoinflammatory disease, and lupus based on age and phenotype.

items.label: PNGD/IGD
items.detail: Target RA, SLE, vasculitis, malignancy, infection, and medication causes.

items.label: Do not order every autoimmune and malignancy test for every lesion
items.detail: The probability of an association depends on age, morphology, blood counts, systemic symptoms, and recurrence.

items.label: Reassess over time
items.detail: A systemic disorder may declare itself after the first skin episode; new symptoms or recurrent disease should reopen the workup.

citations.quote: Review classifies neutrophilic dermatoses by clinical and histopathologic pattern and emphasizes exclusion of infection and systemic associations.
Review defines neutrophilic urticarial dermatosis as transient, usually nonpruritic lesions with dermal neutrophilia, leukocytoclasia, and no vasculitis.
A 65-patient series supports reactive granulomatous dermatitis as an umbrella for IGD, PNGD, and related patterns with frequent systemic associations.
